title: Write computeOutputFileName(), which appends ".counts" to an input file name
notes: observed: re/original-grade-txt/29_outname.grade.txt starts with `Attempting to compile:` and the command after the colon is EMPTY, then three testcase blocks, each `Your output is correct` / `  - Valgrind was clean (no errors, no memory leaks)` / `valgrind was clean`, then `Overall Grade: A`. observed: the README says 'You can make and test with the main function found in outname_test.c' and gives the required signature `char * computeOutputFileName(const char * inputName)` plus the malloc requirement; the Makefile's CFLAGS are `-Wall -Werror -std=gnu99 -pedantic -ggdb3` and its PROGRAM is `outname_test`; 29_outname/outname.c and outname.h are the student's implementation and the teacher's header. recovered: drivers/29_outname/outname_test.c is the teacher driver - its content is the in-directory outname_test.c, and every claim the object makes about it matches (one function `main`, 174 bytes; imports only computeOutputFileName, printf, free, __stack_chk_fail; .rodata "input.txt", "anotherTestFileName.txt", "somethingelse", "'%s' => '%s'\n"; DWARF puts `main(void)` at line 7 and the local `testNames` at line 8, exactly where they are in the source); the reference run prints the three expected lines, stored as configs/expected/29_outname/test.txt. inferred: the driver takes no arguments and reads no files, so the original's three testcases must have been three identical runs of ./outname_test, which is what is configured here; the case labels repeat because the original repeated them. platform substitution: the 2024 grader used valgrind, which does not exist on macOS/arm64 and cannot be installed. `memory_check` builds with AddressSanitizer instead, and the original valgrind wording is kept in the report so the two stay comparable. IMPORTANT caveat, recorded rather than hidden: Apple clang 21 ships no LeakSanitizer (`-fsanitize=leak` is rejected for arm64-apple-darwin, and the ASan runtime answers `detect_leaks is not supported on this platform`), so only the memory-ERROR half of valgrind's verdict is really checked here - a leak-only defect would not be caught. Do not read `or memory leaks` in that line as verified. The reference implementation is ASan-clean (verified with `detect_leaks=0`). Template exclusions: the committed Linux `outname_test` binary and outname_test.o are not part of the starting template; outname_test.c IS kept because the README tells the student to use that main, and outname.c is reduced to its signature plus TODO.
